text.p: Seagull Energy Corp said Wednesday directors increased the 1997 capital expenditures budget by $36 million to a total of $287 million.
The additional funds will be used to sustain the momentum created since late 1996 by the company's exploration and development programs, Chief Executive Barry Galt said.
"Our successes over the last few months have confirmed that we have an abundance of attractive opportunities.
"A majority of the incremental cash will be used to fund additional exploratory and development drilling, primarily within our domestic operations."

The company said it now expects to spend just over $270 million on exploration and production in 1997, with development spending accounting for $152 million, $97 million set aside for exploration and $22 million allocated for leasehold acquisitions. More than $125 million of this spending is targeted outside the United States.

Capital spending outside exploration and production will total about $16 million in 1997, including $9 million by the company's gas transmission and distribution operation in Alaska and the remainder at the corporate level, it said.
In exploration, Galt noted, Seagull will be expanding its onshore program along the Gulf Coast, probably drilling eight or nine more wells than originally planned.

He said the company entered 1997 expecting to drill about 135 development wells, but may now drill some 150 or more. This increased activity will be focused onshore in Texas, Louisiana, Oklahoma and Arkansas.
